description:
The verify verdict cache has ONE reader and TWO writers, and the missing read costs a full suite run on every completing tasklist.

MEASURED on cuneiform 2026-09-02. A tasklist ran the workspace suite TWICE for one merge: once when the agent invoked `.chief/verify.sh` itself inside its turn (~20 minutes, producing /private/tmp/verify-381.log, ending 'all selected gates green — allowing merge'), and again in `_agent_verify_final` on the COMPLETE turn (~21 minutes and still going when this was written). The run showed `iter 2 · no progress last iter (1/2)`: iteration 1 was spent running a verify chief was about to run anyway.

WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT — DO NOT REBUILD IT. `verify_cache_try` / `verify_cache_record` in `engine/lib.sh` are correct, and their key is the right one: `tree.base.hook`, because 'a rebase can rewrite commit ids without changing the tree, so the tree is the correctness key'. `driver.sh:2929` already tries the cache before the merge gate, which is why the MERGE-gate duplicate does not happen. That half of the design works.

THE GAP. `grep -rn 'verify_cache_try' engine/` returns exactly one call site — driver.sh. `_agent_verify_final` (agent.sh:988) calls `run_verify` unconditionally and then `verify_cache_record`. It RECORDS but never TRIES. So a GREEN verdict already on disk for the identical tree, base and hook cannot save it, and no amount of the agent being careful can help: the agent's own invocation is a plain shell command chief never sees.

WHY THIS IS NOT A DOCUMENTATION PROBLEM. `cuneiform/CLAUDE.md` already says 'Never run the full workspace suite inside a chief iteration — commit instead.' It is prose, agents ignore it, and it has now cost a full suite run three times in one day in one repository. The mechanism is the fix.

userStories.title: The final verify consults the cache it already writes
acceptanceCriteria: `_agent_verify_final` calls `verify_cache_try` before `run_verify`, using the same `(cwd, name, base)` triple `verify_cache_record` writes with, so a GREEN verdict for the identical tree/base/hook skips the re-run. Reuse the existing helpers unchanged — this story adds a call, it does not add a cache.

The skip is visible in the log and distinguishable from a fresh pass, which `verify_cache_try` already does ('verify SKIPPED: tree … GREEN verdict from …'). A silent skip would make a stale-cache bug undiagnosable.

A skipped verify is still a PASSED verify for completion purposes — `COMPLETE_OK` is unchanged when the cache hits. Read the `[ "$rc" != 0 ]` branch and make sure a hit takes the same path a fresh green does.
GATES: `bash -n`, `shellcheck -S error`, the behavioral tests, doc-sync, and the version bump the engine-change gate requires.

userStories.title: A recording path the agent can actually use
acceptanceCriteria: An agent-invocable way to run the verify hook that RECORDS its verdict, so an in-turn run populates the cache US-1 now reads. Whether that is a `chief` subcommand or an env-marked wrapper is the implementer's call; what matters is that it is reachable from an agent's shell and writes through `verify_cache_record`.
It is documented where an agent will encounter it — the turn prompt or the verify-hook reference — since the entire point is that the current prose instruction does not work.

It refuses to record a verdict for a tree that is not HEAD's. Recording someone else's tree as green is the one failure mode of this whole mechanism that would let a red tree merge, and it must be impossible rather than unlikely.

userStories.title: Proof it bites, in both directions
acceptanceCriteria: A test proves the skip happens: record a GREEN verdict for a tree, run the final verify at that same tree, assert the hook did NOT execute a second time (count invocations rather than reading the log).

A NEGATIVE CONTROL proves it does not over-skip: change the tree, and assert the hook DOES run. Then change only the verify hook's own content at an unchanged tree, and assert it runs again — the hook blob is part of the key precisely so an edited gate is not skipped by a verdict taken under the old one.
A RED recorded verdict must never skip. `verify_cache_try` already returns non-zero unless `status=0`; assert it, because that is the difference between a cache and a way to merge a failing tree.
